bull.b: Growth across both commercial products indicates expanding demand rather than reliance on a single recent launch. Continued volume gains, higher prescriptions, and raised DAYBUE guidance could support durable revenue growth and operating leverage over the next several quarters.

EU authorization expands DAYBUE’s addressable market and establishes a regulatory foothold beyond the United States. Being the first approved treatment for Rett syndrome in the EU may support physician awareness, patient access, and a new international revenue channel.

A substantial cash balance combined with very low debt gives ACADIA financial flexibility to fund commercialization, advance clinical programs, and pursue business development. This reduces refinancing pressure and improves resilience while the pipeline develops.

bear.b: Positive cash generation is not yet consistently tracking reported profitability. The recent free-cash-flow decline and mixed conversion could limit internally funded investment if the pattern persists, making future operating performance more important to capital allocation.

Higher selling costs can absorb part of the benefit from sales growth, while substantial gross-to-net deductions reduce realized revenue from prescriptions. Together, these pressures may constrain margin expansion and make profitability more sensitive to commercial execution.

The settlement and remaining litigation preserve a legal and governance overhang tied to earlier regulatory setbacks. Ongoing scrutiny may consume management attention, create additional financial or reputational exposure, and weigh on stakeholder confidence over the medium term.
